### website/src/usage-overview.md

# Log files

`rhit` (or `sudo rhit` depending on your configuration) will open the access logs if they're at their standard location.

So you just launch it as

```bash
rhit
```

and go on adding filters and fields as you explore your data.

You may open a specific file, or a specific directory, by giving the path as argument:

```bash
rhit my/archived/logs
```

**Note:**
    Only the default log format is currently supported. Custom logs aren't understood by Rhit.


# Launch parameters

`rhit --help` will display all available launch arguments.

The arguments you'll most often use enable

* [filtering](../usage-filters) hits to focus on a specific subset: `--date`, `--ip`, `--method`, `--path`, `--referer`, `--status`
* [choosing the displayed fields](../usage-fields): `--fields`
* [choosing the sorting key](../usage-key), either *hits* (default) or *bytes*: `--key`
* specifying the detail level, the length of tables: `--length`, from `0` (short) to `6` (long), `1` being the default
* seeing the [recent changes](../usage-changes): `--changes`
* [exporting](../export) the filtered lines, either to screen or to a file



### website/src/usage-fields.md

# The fields argument

Here's a typical access log line:

```no-wrap
178.133.125.122 - - [21/Jan/2021:05:49:52 +0000] "HEAD /broot/download/x86_64-pc-windows-gnu/broot.exe HTTP/1.1" 200 0 "-" "Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1)"
```
Rhit can show tables on the following fields:

* date,
* time,
* method
* status
* (remote) IP
* referer
* path

You can specify the list of fields on which you want sorted tables.

If you specify nothing, the default is to show dates, status, referers and paths.

Fields are refered either by their name (eg `ip`) or by their initial (eg `i`).

The syntax is best explained with a few examples

Goal | Argument
-|-
Only the paths | `--field path` or `-f path` or `-f p`
IP and paths | `-f path+ip` or `-f p+i`
The default fields *and* the IP | `-f +ip` or `-f +i`
The default fields *and* IP and status | `-f +ip+status` or `-f +i+s`
The default fields minus dates | `-f -d`
The default fields with IP but not dates | `-f +i-d`
Default fields but paths moved to the end | `-f +p`
All fields except the paths | `-f all-paths` or `-f a-p`
All the fields, with dates moved to the end | `f all+dates` or `-f a+d`

# Date

This field is shown by an histogram.

You choose it with `--field date`, that you may shorten in `-f date` or `-f d`:

![date](img/fields-date.png)

By default the length of the bars is based on the hit counts (in pink). You may base it on sent bytes by changing the [sorting key](../usage-key).

# Time

This field is shown by an histogram with 24 bars: one per hour.

You choose it with `--field time`, that you may shorten in `-f d`.

Note that the time is the the server's time.

# Remote IP

The remote adresses table isn't displayed by default.

To see it alone use `rhit -f i`.
To see it with default fields, use `rhit -f +i`

![ip](img/fields-ip.png)

As for most fields, you see the number of different values (here the 24,691 remote adresses), the most frequent ones, of for each of them the hits, bytes sent, histogram per day and maybe a trend.

If you want more frequent adresses, use the `--length` field, for example `rhit -l 3`.

# Method

The HTTP method table isn't displayed by default.

To see it use `rhit -f +m`:

![method](img/fields-method.png)

As you'd see by [exporting the lines](../export) with `rhit -m other --lines`, the "other" methods are usually client errors, that is malformed requests.

# Path

The path is displayed by default.

If you want to see only the path, use `rhit -f p`:

![path](img/fields-path.png)

By default some paths are filtered from that tables: the images, scripts, etc.

If you don't want this filter, use the `--all` argument:

![path](img/fields-all-paths.png)

# Referer

The referer is one of the default fields. If you want ot see it alone, do `rhit -f ref`

*(yes, it's called "referer" and not "referrer" in the HTTP protocol, so I'll use this spelling everywhere in this documentation for consistency)*

![referer](img/fields-referer.png)

# Status

The status is one of the default fields. If you want ot see it alone, do `rhit -f status`

![status](img/fields-status.png)

### website/src/usage-filters.md

# The filters arguments

While you may discover some big phenomenas when looking at the unfiltered tables, that's only the surface and you'll normally dive soon enough with filters either because the unfiltered data hinted a something interesting or because you wanted to look at some parts of your sites, or some errors, etc.

So there's a filter argument for each field, and they may be combined.

**Note:**
	On most shells, characters like `$`, `<`, `>`, `|`, or `!` have a special meaning if not between single quotes. In case of doubt put your arguments between quotes, for example `rhit -s '!404'`

# Filter by Date-Time

The date-time filter argument is `--date`, shortened in `-d`.

The order of tokens is year, month (numerical) then day (in 1-31).
If you specify the time, it follows the same logic: hour, minute, seconds.

For example here are the 6 days in the range from `2021/02/15` to `2021/02/20`:

![filter by date](img/filter-date.png)

The filter's behavior is probably better explained with a list of examples:

Purpose|Example
-|-
Show the hits of a specific day | `-d 2021/02/16`
Show the hits of a specific month | `-d 2021/02`
Show the hits of a specific year | `-d 2021`
All days but one | `-d '!2021/02/15'` (don't forget the quotes)
Days after a specific one | `-d '>2021/02/28'`
Days before a specific one | `-d '<2021/02/28'`
Days of a specific range (inclusive) | `-d 2021/11/01-2021/12/25`
Precise range (4 minutes)| `-d 2021/11/01T15:05-2021/11/01T15:08`
Very precise range (a few seconds)| `-d 2021/11/01T15:05:58-2021/11/01T15:06:04`

Shorcuts are sometimes possible. For example if all the log files are from the same year, you may ommit it:

![filter by date no year](img/filter-date-no-year.png)

# Filter by Time

To filter by the time in the day (in the server timezone), use `--time` or `-t`.

For example to get evening hits, use `-t '>18:30'`.

# Filter by Remote IP Address

Remote IP filters are defined with `--ip`, shortened in `-i`.

You may filter to show the hits of a specific IP or the other ones, or do a string based filtering.

Purpose|Example
-|-
Show the hits of a specific IP | `-i 35.180.167.230`
Show all hits but the ones of a specific IP | `-i '!35.180.167.230'`
Show all hits from IP starting with '192' | `-i '^192'`

# Filter by Method

Method filters are defined with `--method`, shortened in `-m`.

You may either filter to show the hits of a specific method or the other ones.

Purpose|Example
-|-
Show the hits of a specific method | `-m CONNECT`
Show all hits but the ones of a specific method | `-m '!POST'`

# Filter by Path

The path filter, defined with `--path` (or `-p`) is the most common one and the most powerful, with a versatile syntax.

The simplest path filter is just a word that the path must contain, for example `-p blog` when you want to see all hits on paths with "blog".

Example:

![filter og/h](img/filter-path-ogh.png)

But it may also be a regular expression, for example all paths with "download" and ending in "exe": `-p 'download.*exe$'`.

You may negate an expression with a `!`. For example all hits not ending in ̀"broot/": `-p '!broot/$'

You may add conditions by separating them with commas. To say you want all downloads, but not the exe and not rhit, you can say `-p download,!rhit,!exe$'

If your query is more complex, use parenthesis and logical operators `&`, `|` and `!` (add parenthesis around operators and parenthesis to avoid them being understood as part of regular expressions).

Here's a list of examples

Example | Meaning
-|-
`-p blog` | path contains "blog"
`-p 'blog.*broot'` | path contains "blog" and "broot", in this order
`-p 'blog,broot'` | path contains "blog" and "broot", in whatever order
`-p '^down/.*broot(.exe)?$'` | path starts with "down" and ends in "broot" with optionally "exe"
`-p 'down/(rh|bro)'` | path contains "down/" immediately followed by either "rh" or "bro"
`-p 'down/bro,!exe$'` | path contains "down/bro" and doesn't end in "exe"
`-p 'og | ( broot & !exe )'` | contains "og" or "broot" without "exe"
`-p '!^/\d+$'` | paths that aren't just a number
`-p '!^/\d+$,!broot'` | paths that aren't a number and don't contain "broot"
`-p 'y & !( \d{4} | sp | bl )'` | path contains "y" but neither a 4 digits number, "sp", nor "bl"

# Filter by Referer

Referer filters are specified with `--referer` or `-r`.

They follow exactly the same syntax than [path filters](#filter-by-path).

Example:

![filter by referer](img/filter-referer.png)

# ---- Field parsing --------------------------------------------------------

def parse_fields(expr: Optional[str]) -> List[str]:
    if not expr:
        return list(DEFAULT_FIELDS)
    fields: List[str] = []
    # If expression starts with + or -, start from defaults; else from empty/all token.
    if expr[0] in "+-":
        fields = list(DEFAULT_FIELDS)
    pos = 0
    op = '+'
    # commas are additions except after a leading all/default state; keep '-' operators.
    while pos < len(expr):
        ch = expr[pos]
        if ch in '+-,':
            op = '-' if ch == '-' else '+'
            pos += 1
            continue
        start = pos
        while pos < len(expr) and expr[pos] not in '+-,':
            pos += 1
        tok = expr[start:pos].strip().lower()
        if not tok:
            continue
        if tok not in FIELD_ALIASES:
            first = tok[0] if tok else ''
            raise CliError(f"error: invalid value '{expr}' for '--fields <FIELDS>': unrecognized field start '{first}'\n")
        fld = FIELD_ALIASES[tok]
        if fld == "all":
            if op == '-':
                fields = []
            else:
                fields = list(ALL_FIELDS)
            continue
        if op == '-':
            fields = [f for f in fields if f != fld]
        else:
            fields = [f for f in fields if f != fld]
            fields.append(fld)
    return fields

# ---- Reading and parsing logs -------------------------------------------

def should_take_name(path: str, no_check: bool) -> bool:
    if no_check:
        return True
    base = os.path.basename(path)
    return "access.log" in base

def discover_files(paths: List[str], no_name_check: bool, default_mode: bool=False) -> Tuple[List[str], str]:
    if not paths:
        paths = ["/var/log/nginx"]
        default_mode = True
    all_files: List[str] = []
    display_root = paths[0] if len(paths) == 1 else paths[0]
    for p in paths:
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            if default_mode:
                sys.stdout.write("No nginx log found at default location, do you have nginx set up?\n")
                sys.stdout.write("If necessary, provide the path to the log file(s) as argument.\n")
                sys.stdout.write("More information with 'rhit --help'.\n")
            raise AppError(f"Error: PathNotFound(\"{p}\")\n")
        if os.path.isdir(p):
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(p):
                # Keep platform directory order as much as possible; don't force sorting.
                for name in files:
                    fp = os.path.join(root, name)
                    if should_take_name(fp, no_name_check):
                        all_files.append(fp)
        else:
            all_files.append(p)
    return all_files, display_root

def open_text(path: str):
    if path.endswith(".gz"):
        return gzip.open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    return open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

def parse_line(line: str, file_index: int, line_index: int) -> Optional[Hit]:
    raw = line.rstrip("\n")
    m = LOG_RE.search(raw)
    if not m:
        return None
    dm = DT_RE.match(m.group("dt"))
    if not dm:
        return None
    day, mon_s, year, hh, mm, ss = dm.groups()
    mon = MONTHS.get(mon_s)
    if not mon:
        return None
    try:
        dt = datetime(int(year), mon, int(day), int(hh), int(mm), int(ss))
        bytes_sent = int(m.group("bytes"))
    except Exception:
        return None
    req = m.group("req")
    parts = req.split()
    if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[2].startswith("HTTP/"):
        raw_method = parts[0]
        path = parts[1]
        method = raw_method if raw_method in KNOWN_METHODS else "other"
    else:
        method = "none"
        path = req
    if "?" in path:
        path = path.split("?", 1)[0]
    return Hit(raw=raw, dt=dt, ip=m.group("ip"), method=method, path=path,
               status=m.group("status"), bytes=bytes_sent, referer=m.group("ref"),
               file_index=file_index, line_index=line_index)

def read_logs(paths: List[str], opts: Options) -> Tuple[List[Hit], int, str]:
    files, display_root = discover_files(paths, opts.no_name_check, default_mode=(len(paths)==0))
    log_files: List[LogFile] = []
    for order, fp in enumerate(files):
        hits: List[Hit] = []
        try:
            with open_text(fp) as f:
                for li, line in enumerate(f):
                    h = parse_line(line, order, li)
                    if h:
                        hits.append(h)
        except Exception as e:
            # The original reports many IO/flate failures through Debug; keep concise.
            raise AppError(f"Error: {type(e).__name__}(\"{fp}\")\n")
        if hits:
            log_files.append(LogFile(fp, hits, order))
    if not log_files:
        raise AppError("Error: NoLogFileFound\n")
    # Observed exports sort log files chronologically, but keep line order inside each file.
    log_files.sort(key=lambda lf: (lf.hits[0].dt, lf.order))
    out: List[Hit] = []
    for n, lf in enumerate(log_files):
        for h in lf.hits:
            h.file_index = n
            out.append(h)
    return out, len(log_files), display_root

# ---- Filters --------------------------------------------------------------

class DateFilter:
    def __init__(self, pattern: str, all_hits: List[Hit]):

        self.neg = False
        p = pattern.strip()
        if p.startswith('!'):
            self.neg = True; p = p[1:]
        self.op = 'exact'
        self.start: Optional[datetime] = None
        self.end: Optional[datetime] = None
        self.valid_span_for_table = False
        base = all_hits[0].dt if all_hits else datetime.now()
        try:
            if p.startswith('>') or p.startswith('<'):
                self.op = p[0]
                a, b = parse_date_span(p[1:], base)
                if self.op == '>':
                    self.start = b
                else:
                    self.end = a
            elif '-' in p:
                left, right = p.split('-', 1)
                self.start = parse_date_span(left, base)[0]
                self.end = parse_date_span(right, base)[1]
                self.op = 'range'
                self.valid_span_for_table = not self.neg
            else:
                self.start, self.end = parse_date_span(p, base)
                self.valid_span_for_table = not self.neg

            ok = dt < self.end
        else:

        return not ok if self.neg else ok

def parse_int_token(tok: str) -> int:
    if not tok or not re.match(r'^\d+$', tok):
        # close enough for observed errors
        if tok and '-' in tok:
            raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: PosOverflow }))\n")
        raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: Empty }))\n")
    return int(tok)

def last_day_of_month(year: int, month: int) -> int:
    if month == 12:
        nxt = date(year+1, 1, 1)
    else:
        nxt = date(year, month+1, 1)
    return (nxt - timedelta(days=1)).day

def parse_date_span(s: str, base: datetime) -> Tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    s = s.strip()
    if not s:
        raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: Empty }))\n")
    date_part, time_part = (s.split('T', 1) + [None])[:2] if 'T' in s else (s, None)
    comps = date_part.split('/') if date_part else []
    # Shortcuts: YYYY, YYYY/MM, YYYY/MM/DD; MM/DD; DD
    try:
        nums = [int(c) for c in comps if c != '']
    except ValueError:
        raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: Empty }))\n")
    if len(nums) != len(comps) or not nums:
        raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: Empty }))\n")
    if len(nums) == 1:
        if len(comps[0]) == 4:
            year, month, day = nums[0], 1, 1; gran = 'year'
        else:
            year, month, day = base.year, base.month, nums[0]; gran = 'day'
    elif len(nums) == 2:
        if len(comps[0]) == 4:
            year, month, day = nums[0], nums[1], 1; gran = 'month'
        else:
            year, month, day = base.year, nums[0], nums[1]; gran = 'day'
    else:
        year, month, day = nums[0], nums[1], nums[2]; gran = 'day'
    h = mi = sec = 0
    tgran = None
    if time_part is not None:
        tcomps = time_part.split(':')
        try:
            vals = [int(c) for c in tcomps if c != '']
        except ValueError:
            raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: Empty }))\n")
        if len(vals) != len(tcomps) or not vals:
            raise AppError("Error: DateTime(IntExpected(ParseIntError { kind: Empty }))\n")
        h = vals[0]
        if len(vals) > 1: mi = vals[1]
        if len(vals) > 2: sec = vals[2]
        tgran = ['hour','minute','second'][min(len(vals),3)-1]
    start = datetime(year, month, day, h, mi, sec)
    if tgran == 'second':
        end = start
    elif tgran == 'minute':
        end = start.replace(second=59)
    elif tgran == 'hour':
        end = start.replace(minute=59, second=59)
    elif gran == 'day':
        end = start.replace(hour=23, minute=59, second=59)
    elif gran == 'month':
        end = datetime(year, month, last_day_of_month(year, month), 23, 59, 59)
    else:
        end = datetime(year, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59)
    return start, end

class TimeFilter:
    def __init__(self, pattern: str):
        p = pattern.strip()
        if p.startswith('>') or p.startswith('<'):
            self.op = p[0]
            self.a = parse_clock(p[1:])
            self.b = None
        elif '-' in p:
            self.op = 'range'
            left, right = p.split('-', 1)
            self.a = parse_clock(left)
            self.b = parse_clock(right)
        else:
            raise AppError("Error: TimeFilter(InvalidFormat)\n")
    def match(self, h: Hit) -> bool:
        seconds = h.dt.hour*3600 + h.dt.minute*60 + h.dt.second
        if self.op == '>': return seconds > self.a
        if self.op == '<': return seconds < self.a
        return self.a <= seconds <= self.b

def parse_clock(s: str) -> int:
    parts = s.strip().split(':')
    if not (1 <= len(parts) <= 3):
        raise AppError("Error: TimeFilter(InvalidFormat)\n")
    try:
        h = int(parts[0]); m = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) >= 2 else 0
        # seconds in the argument are accepted but ignored by the observed program
        sec = 0
    except Exception:
        raise AppError("Error: TimeFilter(InvalidFormat)\n")
    return h*3600 + m*60 + sec

class StatusFilter:
    def __init__(self, pattern: str):
        self.pattern = pattern
        self.pos: List[Tuple[int,int]] = []
        self.neg: List[Tuple[int,int]] = []
        for raw in pattern.split(','):
            tok = raw.strip()
            if not tok: continue
            neg = tok.startswith('!')
            if neg: tok = tok[1:].strip()
            try:
                rng = parse_status_token(tok)
            except ValueError:
                raise AppError("Error: StatusFilter(ParseInt(ParseIntError { kind: InvalidDigit }))\n")
            (self.neg if neg else self.pos).append(rng)
    def match(self, h: Hit) -> bool:
        st = int(h.status)
        ok = True if not self.pos else any(a <= st <= b for a,b in self.pos)
        if any(a <= st <= b for a,b in self.neg):
            ok = False
        return ok

def parse_status_token(tok: str) -> Tuple[int,int]:
    if len(tok) == 3 and tok[0].isdigit() and tok[1:].lower() == 'xx':
        c = int(tok[0]); return c*100, c*100+99
    if '-' in tok:
        a,b = tok.split('-',1); return int(a), int(b)
    v = int(tok); return v, v

class RegexFilter:
    def __init__(self, pattern: str):
        self.pattern = pattern
        try:
            self.func = compile_expr(pattern)
        except re.error as e:
            raise AppError(regex_error(pattern, str(e)))
    def match(self, text: str) -> bool:
        return self.func(text)

def regex_error(pat: str, msg: str) -> str:
    # Rust's regex crate has a detailed pretty diagnostic. Reproduce the common shape.
    return (
        "Error: StrFilter(InvalidRegex(Syntax(\n"
        "~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n"
        "regex parse error:\n"
        f"    {pat!r}\n"
        "     ^\n"
        f"error: {msg}\n"
        "~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n"
        ")))\n"
    )

def compile_simple_regex(pat: str) -> Callable[[str], bool]:
    r = re.compile(pat)
    return lambda s: r.search(s) is not None

def compile_expr(expr: str) -> Callable[[str], bool]:
    expr = expr.strip()
    # Commas are AND separators at top level in the documented syntax.
    parts = split_top_commas(expr)
    if len(parts) > 1:
        funcs = [compile_expr(p) for p in parts]
        return lambda s: all(f(s) for f in funcs)
    # Whitespace-separated boolean operators. No-space | or (...) stays a regex.
    tokens = bool_tokens(expr)
    if any(t in ('&','|','(',')') for t in tokens) or any(t == '!' for t in tokens):
        parser = BoolParser(tokens)
        return parser.parse()
    if expr.startswith('!'):
        f = compile_simple_regex(expr[1:])
        return lambda s: not f(s)
    return compile_simple_regex(expr)

def split_top_commas(s: str) -> List[str]:
    out=[]; cur=[]; depth=0
    for ch in s:
        if ch == '(' and (not cur or cur[-1].isspace()): depth += 1
        elif ch == ')' and depth: depth -= 1
        if ch == ',' and depth == 0:
            out.append(''.join(cur).strip()); cur=[]
        else:
            cur.append(ch)
    out.append(''.join(cur).strip())
    return [p for p in out if p]

def bool_tokens(s: str) -> List[str]:
    toks=[]
    # Only treat operators as boolean when separated by whitespace or parenthesis tokens.
    for part in s.split():
        # peel leading ! and parens written as separate-ish tokens: !( or (foo is left regex unless exactly paren form
        while part and part[0] in '(!' and (part[0] == '!' or part == '(' or part.startswith('(')):
            if part[0] == '!': toks.append('!'); part = part[1:]
            elif part[0] == '(' and (len(part)==1 or part[1:].strip()):
                toks.append('('); part = part[1:]
            else: break
        trail=[]
        while part.endswith(')') and len(part) > 1:
            part = part[:-1]; trail.append(')')
        if part in ('&','|','(',')','!'):
            toks.append(part)
        elif part:
            toks.append(part)
        toks.extend(trail)
    return toks if toks else [s]

class BoolParser:
    def __init__(self, tokens: List[str]): self.tokens=tokens; self.i=0
    def peek(self): return self.tokens[self.i] if self.i < len(self.tokens) else None
    def pop(self): t=self.peek(); self.i+=1; return t
    def parse(self):
        f=self.parse_or()
        return f
    def parse_or(self):
        f=self.parse_and()
        while self.peek() == '|':
            self.pop(); g=self.parse_and(); f=(lambda f=f,g=g: lambda s: f(s) or g(s))()
        return f
    def parse_and(self):
        f=self.parse_not()
        while self.peek() == '&':
            self.pop(); g=self.parse_not(); f=(lambda f=f,g=g: lambda s: f(s) and g(s))()
        return f
    def parse_not(self):
        if self.peek() == '!':
            self.pop(); f=self.parse_not(); return lambda s: not f(s)
        return self.parse_atom()
    def parse_atom(self):
        t=self.pop()
        if t == '(':
            f=self.parse_or()
            if self.peek() == ')': self.pop()
            return f
        if t is None:
            return lambda s: True
        if t == ')':
            return lambda s: True
        return compile_simple_regex(t)

def method_matcher(pattern: str) -> Callable[[Hit], bool]:
    neg = pattern.startswith('!')
    p = pattern[1:] if neg else pattern
    p = p.upper() if p.upper() in KNOWN_METHODS else p
    if p not in KNOWN_METHODS and p not in ('none', 'other'):
        p = 'other'
    def fn(h: Hit) -> bool:
        ok = (h.method == p)
        return not ok if neg else ok
    return fn

def build_filter_plan(opts: Options, all_hits: List[Hit]):
    plan=[]
    if opts.date_filter is not None:
        df = DateFilter(opts.date_filter, all_hits); plan.append(('date', opts.date_filter, lambda h,df=df: df.match(h), df))
    if opts.ip_filter is not None:
        rf = RegexFilter(opts.ip_filter); plan.append(('IP', opts.ip_filter, lambda h,rf=rf: rf.match(h.ip), None))
    if opts.method_filter is not None:
        mf = method_matcher(opts.method_filter); plan.append(('method', opts.method_filter, mf, None))
    if opts.path_filter is not None:
        rf = RegexFilter(opts.path_filter); plan.append(('path', opts.path_filter, lambda h,rf=rf: rf.match(h.path), None))
    if opts.referer_filter is not None:
        rf = RegexFilter(opts.referer_filter); plan.append(('referer', opts.referer_filter, lambda h,rf=rf: rf.match(h.referer), None))
    if opts.status_filter is not None:
        sf = StatusFilter(opts.status_filter); plan.append(('status', opts.status_filter, lambda h,sf=sf: sf.match(h), None))
    if opts.time_filter is not None:
        tf = TimeFilter(opts.time_filter); plan.append(('time', opts.time_filter, lambda h,tf=tf: tf.match(h), None))
    return plan

def apply_filters(hits: List[Hit], plan):
    cur = hits
    stats=[]
    for name, pat, fn, obj in plan:
        before = len(cur)
        cur = [h for h in cur if fn(h)]
        removed = before - len(cur)
        pct = (removed * 100.0 / before) if before else 0.0
        stats.append((name, pat, pct))
    return cur, stats

def row_cap(length: int) -> int:
    if length <= 0: return 10
    return min(300, 50 * max(1, length))

def metric(hits: int, byt: int, key: str) -> int:
    return byt if key == 'bytes' else hits

def fmt_pct(n: int, total: int) -> str:
    if total == 0:
        return "0.0%"
    return f"{n*100.0/total:.1f}%"

def is_resource(path: str) -> bool:
    # Strip final query already done; look at lower-case extension after last slash/dot.
    last = path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1].lower()
    if '.' not in last:
        return False
    ext = last.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]
    return ext in RESOURCE_EXTS

def aggregate(hits: List[Hit], field: str, all_paths: bool=False):
    d: Dict[str, List[int]] = {}
    for h in hits:
        if field == 'status': val = h.status
        elif field == 'ref':
            val = h.referer
            if val == '-' or val == '': continue
        elif field == 'path':
            val = h.path
            if not all_paths and is_resource(val): continue
        elif field == 'ip': val = h.ip
        elif field == 'method': val = h.method
        else: val = ''
        if val not in d: d[val] = [0,0]
        d[val][0] += 1; d[val][1] += h.bytes
    return d

def sort_items(agg: Dict[str, List[int]], key: str):
    return sorted(agg.items(), key=lambda kv: (-metric(kv[1][0], kv[1][1], key), kv[0]))

def table_line(widths: List[int], left: str, sep: str, right: str, fill: str='─') -> str:
    return left + sep.join(fill*w for w in widths) + right

def align(text: str, width: int, how: str='left') -> str:
    if len(text) > width:
        text = text[:width]
    if how == 'right': return text.rjust(width)
    if how == 'center': return text.center(width)
    return text.ljust(width)

def wrap_cell(text: str, width: int) -> List[str]:
    if width <= 0: return ['']
    if text == '': return ['']
    return [text[i:i+width] for i in range(0, len(text), width)] or ['']

def render_table(headers: List[str], rows: List[List[Tuple[str,str]]], widths: List[int]) -> str:
    # rows are [(text, align), ...]
    out=[]
    out.append(table_line(widths, '┌', '┬', '┐'))
    # header may wrap too
    hrows = [wrap_cell(h, widths[i]) for i,h in enumerate(headers)]
    maxh = max(len(x) for x in hrows)
    for k in range(maxh):
        cells=[]
        for i,h in enumerate(headers):
            part = hrows[i][k] if k < len(hrows[i]) else ''
            cells.append(align(part, widths[i], 'center' if h in ('#','%') else 'left'))
        out.append('│' + '│'.join(cells) + '│')
    out.append(table_line(widths, '├', '┼', '┤'))
    for row in rows:
        wrapped=[wrap_cell(txt, widths[i]) for i,(txt,al) in enumerate(row)]
        maxr=max(len(x) for x in wrapped)
        for k in range(maxr):
            cells=[]
            for i,(txt,al) in enumerate(row):
                part = wrapped[i][k] if k < len(wrapped[i]) else ''
                cells.append(align(part, widths[i], al if k==0 else ('left' if i==1 else al)))
            out.append('│' + '│'.join(cells) + '│')
    out.append(table_line(widths, '└', '┴', '┘'))
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

def render_simple_value_table(title: str, label: str, agg: Dict[str,List[int]], hits_total: int, opts: Options) -> str:
    items = sort_items(agg, opts.key)[:row_cap(opts.length)]
    count = len(agg)
    out = title + "\n"
    # value column constrained like observed terminal tables
    max_val_len = max([len(label)] + [len(k) for k,_ in items]) if items else len(label)
    val_w = min(max_val_len, 29)
    num_w = max(3, len(str(len(items))))
    hits_w = max(4, max([len(str(v[0])) for _,v in items] + [4]))
    pct_w = max(3, max([len(fmt_pct(v[0], hits_total)) for _,v in items] + [3]))
    bytes_w = max(5, max([len(str(v[1])) for _,v in items] + [5]))
    widths=[num_w, val_w, hits_w, pct_w, bytes_w]
    rows=[]
    for idx,(val,(hc,bc)) in enumerate(items,1):
        rows.append([(str(idx),'right'), (val,'left'), (str(hc),'right'), (fmt_pct(hc,hits_total),'right'), (str(bc),'right')])
    out += render_table(['#', label, 'hits', '%', 'bytes'], rows, widths)
    return out

def block_bar(value: int, maxv: int, width: int=20, chars: str='▏▎▍▌▋▊▉█') -> str:
    if maxv <= 0 or value <= 0:
        return ' ' * width
    x = value / maxv * width
    full = int(x)
    frac = int(round((x - full) * 8))
    if frac >= 8:
        full += 1; frac = 0
    if full > width:
        full = width; frac = 0
    s = '█' * full
    if frac > 0 and len(s) < width:
        s += chars[frac-1]
    return s.ljust(width)

def render_date_table(hits: List[Hit], opts: Options, all_hits: List[Hit], date_filter_obj: Optional[DateFilter]) -> str:
    if date_filter_obj and date_filter_obj.valid_span_for_table and date_filter_obj.start and date_filter_obj.end:
        start_d = date_filter_obj.start.date(); end_d = date_filter_obj.end.date()
    else:
        base = all_hits if all_hits else hits
        if not base: return ''
        start_d = min(h.dt.date() for h in base); end_d = max(h.dt.date() for h in base)
    by: Dict[date, List[int]] = {}
    d = start_d
    while d <= end_d:
        by[d] = [0,0]
        d += timedelta(days=1)
    for h in hits:
        dd = h.dt.date()
        if dd in by:
            by[dd][0]+=1; by[dd][1]+=h.bytes
    rows_data=[]
    maxkey=0
    for dd in sorted(by):
        hc,bc=by[dd]
        maxkey=max(maxkey, metric(hc,bc,opts.key))
        rows_data.append((dd.strftime('%Y/%m/%d'), hc, bc))
    max_label=str(maxkey)
    bar_w=20
    last_header=('0' + max_label.rjust(bar_w-1))[-bar_w:]
    widths=[10, max(4, max([len(str(r[1])) for r in rows_data]+[4])), max(5,max([len(str(r[2])) for r in rows_data]+[5])), bar_w]
    rows=[]
    for ds,hc,bc in rows_data:
        rows.append([(ds,'left'), (str(hc),'right'), (str(bc),'right'), (block_bar(metric(hc,bc,opts.key), maxkey, bar_w),'left')])
    return render_table(['date','hits','bytes',last_header], rows, widths)

def render_time_table(hits: List[Hit], opts: Options) -> str:
    by={h:[0,0] for h in range(24)}

def status_class_table(hits: List[Hit]) -> str:

def render_value_with_changes(field: str, hits: List[Hit], opts: Options, all_paths: bool, days: List[date]) -> str:

        data[val][0]+=1; data[val][1]+=h.bytes
        if h.dt.date() in idx: data[val][2][idx[h.dt.date()]] += metric(1,h.bytes,opts.key)
    items=[]
    for val,(hc,bc,per) in data.items():
        half=max(1,len(per)//2)
        old=sum(per[:-2]) / max(1,len(per[:-2])) if len(per)>2 else 0
        recent=sum(per[-2:]) / min(2,len(per)) if per else 0
        score=recent-old
        items.append((val,hc,bc,per,score))
    normal=sorted(items, key=lambda x:(-metric(x[1],x[2],opts.key), x[0]))
    count=len(data)
    title,label=title_for(field,count,all_paths)
    # changes style titles don't end with a period in observed output
    if field=='path' and not all_paths:
        title=f"{count} paths (excluding resources like images, css, \netc.)"
    elif field=='path': title=f"{count} paths"
    elif field=='ref': title=f"{count} referrers"
    elif field=='ip': title=f"{count} remote IP addresses"
    out=render_changes_table(title,label,normal,days,opts)
    more=sorted(items, key=lambda x:(-x[4], -metric(x[1],x[2],opts.key), x[0]))
    less=sorted(items, key=lambda x:(x[4], -metric(x[1],x[2],opts.key), x[0]))
    mt,label=title_for(field,count,all_paths,modifier='More popular')
    lt,label=title_for(field,count,all_paths,modifier='Less popular')
    out += render_changes_table(mt,label,more,days,opts)
    out += render_changes_table(lt,label,less,days,opts)
    return out


def render_tables(hits: List[Hit], all_hits: List[Hit], opts: Options, filter_stats, plan) -> str:
    total_hits = len(all_hits)
    total_bytes = sum(h.bytes for h in all_hits)
    min_d = min(h.dt.date() for h in all_hits)
    max_d = max(h.dt.date() for h in all_hits)
    out = f"{total_hits} hits and {total_bytes} from {min_d.strftime('%Y/%m/%d')} to {max_d.strftime('%Y/%m/%d')}\n"
    for name,pat,pct in filter_stats:
        msg = f"Filtering by {name} on pattern {pat} removed {pct:.2f}% of total lines"
        out += "\n".join(textwrap.wrap(msg, width=55, break_long_words=False)) + "\n"
    if filter_stats:
        out += f" ==> hits: {len(hits)}, bytes sent: {sum(h.bytes for h in hits)}\n"
    if not hits:
        return out
    fields = parse_fields(opts.fields_expr)
    # date filter object if any
    dfo=None
    for name,pat,fn,obj in plan:
        if name=='date': dfo=obj
    # day list for changes
    start = min(h.dt.date() for h in hits); end = max(h.dt.date() for h in hits)
    days=[]; d=start
    while d<=end:
        days.append(d); d+=timedelta(days=1)
    use_changes = opts.changes and len(days) >= 8
    for f in fields:
        if f == 'date':
            out += render_date_table(hits, opts, all_hits, dfo)
        elif f == 'time':
            out += render_time_table(hits, opts)
        elif f == 'status' and opts.length <= 0:
            out += status_class_table(hits)
        elif f in ('status','method','ip','ref','path'):
            if use_changes and f in ('ip','ref','path'):
                out += render_value_with_changes(f,hits,opts,opts.all_paths,days)
            else:
                agg=aggregate(hits,f,opts.all_paths)
                title,label=title_for(f,len(agg),opts.all_paths)
                out += render_simple_value_table(title,label,agg,len(hits),opts)
    return out

# ---- Color and progress ---------------------------------------------------

def wants_color(opts: Options) -> bool:
    if opts.color == 'yes': return True
    if opts.color == 'no': return False
    return sys.stdout.isatty()

def colorize_tables(s: str) -> str:
    # Lightweight color approximation: boxes grey, key digits pink. Exact styling isn't
    # needed for redirected auto output, but --color yes should visibly style output.
    s = re.sub(r'([┌┬┐├┼┤└┴┘│─]+)', lambda m: '\x1b[38;5;239m'+m.group(1)+'\x1b[39m', s)
    return s

def progress_prefix(file_count: int) -> str:
    return f"\x1b7   0 / {file_count}                                         \x1b8"

def progress_suffix(file_count: int, root: str) -> str:
    bar='████████████████████████████████████████'
    return f"\x1b7   {file_count} / {file_count} {bar}\x1b8\x1b7\x1b8I've read {file_count} file{'s' if file_count != 1 else ''} in \"{root}\"\n"

# ---- Main -----------------------------------------------------------------

def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    try:
        opts = parse_args(argv)
        # paths default handled in read_logs
        hits_all, file_count, root = read_logs(opts.files, opts)
        plan = build_filter_plan(opts, hits_all)
        hits, stats = apply_filters(hits_all, plan)
        if opts.output == 'raw':
            body = output_raw(hits)
        elif opts.output == 'csv':
            body = output_csv(hits)
        elif opts.output == 'json':
            body = output_json(hits)
        else:
            body = render_tables(hits, hits_all, opts, stats, plan)
            if wants_color(opts): body = colorize_tables(body)
        if not opts.silent_load:
            # Keep the original's cursor-save progress flavour. CSV header was observed
            # before progress; preserving exact interleaving is less useful than avoiding
            # hidden stderr writes, but this is close for human use.
            sys.stdout.write(progress_prefix(file_count))
            sys.stdout.write(body)
            sys.stdout.write(progress_suffix(file_count, root))
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(body)
        return 0
    except SystemExit as e:
        return int(e.code or 0)
    except CliError as e:
        sys.stdout.write(e.message)
        return e.code
    except AppError as e:
        sys.stdout.write(e.message)
        return e.code

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
